title: Voices to Velocity: mapping feedback to small-win backlog (May 2028)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact synthesis of customer feedback collected during Apr–May 2028 (support tickets, field conversations, and product interviews). The goal: convert high-signal micro-requests into a prioritized, trackable 'small-win' backlog that product and engineering can action within a 2–6 week cycle. Emphasis on fixes that reduce customer friction for Dedicated/Private users and improve perceived reliability for Hosted API customers.

Methodology summary:
- Source mix: 42 tickets flagged as high-impact by CS reps, 6 post-call notes from solutions eng, two NPS follow-ups, and telemetry-sampled error traces.
- Grouping: clustered by behavioral impact (blocker, repeat-friction, cost surprise, latency regressions), then mapped to ownership (runtime, routing, console, docs).
- Quick-estimates: each item has a simple size/impact tag: size={S,M,L} (dev effort), impact={1–5} (customer pain).

Executive snapshot (top 6 small-win candidates):
1) API 400 on long system prompts (S / impact 4) — multiple customers hit a validation crash when system messages exceed 12k chars. Repro steps in JIRA CS-4127. Low effort: validate and surface clearer error with example fix in SDKs. Owner: hosted-api.
2) KV cache miss telemetry tag (S / impact 3) — customers on Dedicated reported unexplained token cost spikes; telemetry shows misattributed cache misses when rollout model variant changes. Action: add a KV-cache-miss tag to traces and a short console alert. Owner: serving-runtime + observability.
3) Cost estimate preview on Console route config (M / impact 5) — customers surprised by token cost when combining streaming + function calling. Small UX and back-end calc to show per-minute and per-request estimates during config. Owner: console-and-rollouts.
4) Canary fallback visibility (S / impact 4) — teams want a short audit line in console showing which fallback model served a request and why. Add a single-line history entry per route + expand in logs. Owner: console/rollouts & platform-engineering.
5) Default batching behavior doc + toggle (S / impact 2) — confusion: default batching thresholds lead to throttled latency for low-volume routes. Quick doc plus an on/off toggle in route config to disable batching. Owner: serving-runtime + developer-experience.
6) Embedding dimensionality mismatch warning (S / impact 3) — embedding clients get silent down-stepping when model variants change vector size. Add a pre-flight check in embeddings endpoint returning a clear explanatory message. Owner: hosted-api.

Representative customer quotes (verbatim-ish):
- "We got a 400 and our upstream crashed — the error says 'invalid payload' but we have no hint which field." (SaaS analytics startup, Dedicated)
- "Costs spiked overnight, we thought it was a prompt issue — turns out the variant switched and cache evictions went wild." (Fintech platform, Private)
- "The console shows the route as healthy but our user saw a 2–3x latency blip during the canary window." (Large enterprise)

Triage rationale and velocity mapping:
- Priority rule: (impact >=4 AND size != L) OR (repeat-friction across >=3 customers) -> schedule in next 2-week sprint.
- Low-effort, high-impact items (1,2,4,5,6 above) are marked S and suggested for the upcoming sprint. Item 3 (cost preview) is M but high impact; flag for sprint + design spike.

Suggested backlog entries (short-form for direct copy to Jira):
- CS-NEW-01: "Improve system prompt error message (validate length, return actionable guidance)" — size S, owner: hosted-api, due: 2w.
- CS-NEW-02: "Add KV cache miss telemetry and console alert" — size S, owner: serving-runtime/observability, due: 2w.
- CS-NEW-03: "Show route cost-preview during stream/function config" — size M, owner: console-and-rollouts, due: 3–4w (design + small backend).
- CS-NEW-04: "Add canary fallback audit line in route history" — size S, owner: console/rollouts, due: 2w.
- CS-NEW-05: "Batching toggle + doc for route config" — size S, owner: developer-experience/serving-runtime, due: 1–2w.
- CS-NEW-06: "Embeddings pre-flight dimensionality check" — size S, owner: hosted-api, due: 1–2w.

Cross-team quick notes (engineering questions & dependencies):
- serving-runtime: The KV cache miss tagging needs a lightweight trace attribute — can we add this flag without touching hot path token accounting? (Action: runtime to confirm in 3 days).
- console: The cost preview calculation requires short-lived price table access for streaming configs — ops to confirm cost table read SLA.
- developer-experience: Provide short SDK snippet for system-prompt mitigation in two languages (Python, Node).

Risk flags and guardrails:
- Avoid naive batching toggle that silently kills autoscaling efficiency. Toggle must include explanatory tooltip and recommended defaults.
- Embedding size warning should not block the request by default — only warn and provide migration steps, with an opt-in strict mode.

Fast experiments to validate impact (week 0–2):
- Push console audit line behind a feature flag for 10% of routes and collect CS noise reduction metric (tickets referencing 'fallback' or 'canary').
- Release a minimal 1-paragraph doc + SDK snippet for system prompt length; measure reduction in 'invalid payload' follow-ups.

Owner commitments (recommended):
- CS: maintain the mapping spreadsheet and update weekly with new tickets that fit the small-win criteria.
- Eng leads: review S-sized items in sprint planning and commit a single S per team per sprint.
- PM: pick 1 M-sized item to scope and seed design for the month.

Open questions (need quick alignment):
- Do we want a centralized small-win board in Confluence or an engineering-visible Jira filter? (Recommend Jira filter + Confluence one-pager.)
- How aggressive should the KV-cache telemetry be for Dedicated vs Hosted? (Ops/regulatory constraints?)

Appendix: quick signal excerpts and trace refs
- Ticket CS-1791: stack trace snippet + err payload (attached in linked artifacts).
- Field note 2028-05-04 (Ethan): customer demo transcript where cost surprise led to pause in procurement conversation.

Next steps (this week):
- CS to convert the six suggested backlog entries into Jira drafts (owner + acceptance criteria) — due 2028-05-24.
- Runtime and Observability to confirm feasibility and cost of KV-miss tag by 2028-05-25.
- Console PM to triage cost-preview scope and sync with design by 2028-05-26.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally concise; it's designed as a handoff artifact to accelerate low-risk improvements. If you disagree with prioritization, add comments inline in Confluence or ping @Maya in Slack.

-- End of synthesis --
